By the rule *acaḥ parasmin*, [the substitution] will not take effect because of its status as a *sthānivadbhāva* substitute. Nor does the exception "it is not like the original with respect to a rule concerning a word-final element" apply here, because that would result in mutual dependence (*itaretarāśrayatva*).

If the prohibition of *sthānivadbhāva* (the treatment as the original) is present, then there is the status of being a word-final (*padāntatva*); and if there is the status of being a word-final, then there is the prohibition of *sthānivadbhāva*.
[Objection: Even so, because of the rule "that which is not established in what precedes it does not behave like the original" (*pūrvatrāsiddhīye na sthānivat*), *sthānivadbhāva* would not apply.
[Response: It is said in reply:

Furthermore, because of the prohibition against *pratyayalakṣaṇa* (treating a suffix as present for grammatical operations) when the status of being a "word" (*pada*) must be applied to the following member by the rule *uttarapadatve cāpadādividhau*, this [suffix] does not possess the status of a word; therefore, how could there be the elision of the *n*?

If that is so, then the explanation given in the *Vṛtti* on the rule *ṣātpadāntāt*—namely, that this is a locative compound (*saptamīsamāsa*) meaning "at the end of a word" (*pade'ntaḥ*), and that for this reason [the rule] does not apply here in cases such as *susarpiṣkeṇa* and *suyajuṣkeṇa*—is inconsistent.
For it is as follows:

Just as in the example *susarpiṣkeṇa*, where the suffix *ka* follows [the word *susarpiḥ*], the letter *ṣ* remains at the end of what is not a *pada* (an *apada*), and thus the *ṣ* at the end of that form likewise retains its status as being at the end of an *apada*.
It is said in reply:
by the term "rule concerning the beginning of a *pada*," those rules starting from *sātpadādyoḥ* (Pāṇini 8.3.111) are understood.
Therefore, by the statement "in the application of [rules concerning] non-padas and so forth," the status of being a *pada* indeed applies to the subsequent element.
Regarding this point, the inclusion of the term *padānta* (end of a word) in the rule *ṣātpadāntāt* (Pāṇini 8.3.110) is the indicator (*jñāpaka*).
And likewise, Maitreya states in the context of the rule *padavyavāye’pi* (Pāṇini 8.4.38).
And here there is an indicator (*jñāpaka*):
in the rule *ṣātpadāntāt*, the inclusion of the term "end of a word" (*padānta*) for the purpose of defining it as "the end of a word" (*pade antaḥ*) would not be possible otherwise.
To this it is replied: Now, if the inclusion of the term "end of a word" (padānta) is for this purpose, then why not omit it and simply say *ṣāt supi*?
Or rather, one might say *ṣāt pada*.

And this meaning—that the *ṣakāra* which occurs after a word ending in a case-suffix (*subanta*) [is treated as being] before a word (*pada*)—will serve as an indicator (*jñāpaka*) for the stated sense. Furthermore, there is no purpose in such an indication;
let it simply be that "the status of a suffix (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*) applies" in the rule *ṣātpadāntāt* (Pāṇini 8.3.106), rather than [stating] "after a *ṣakāra* at the end of a word."
It is said: as for what was stated—
that one should either say "supi" or "pade"— [it is not necessary].
That is not so;
if that [explanation] holds, then why would the mention of "the end of a word" (padānta) contradict the indication of the aforementioned meaning?
The second [alternative] is also not tenable;

for if such a meaning were conveyed, then in examples such as *druṇasaḥ* and *vārddhrīṇasaḥ*, the substitution of *ṇ* would occur in the word *naḥ* at the end of the compound because of the rule *pūrvapadāt saṃjñāyām agaḥ* (Pāṇini 8.4.3), whereas in *carmanāsikaḥ* there would be no substitution of *ṇ*.
Otherwise, just as in *mātṛbhogīṇaḥ*, there would also have to be a substitution of *ṇ* in *carmanāsikaḥ*.
Likewise, in the compound *māṣakumbhavāpena*, the subsequent word *kumbha* attains the status of a *pada*.
Consequently, in the expression *māṣakumbhavāpena*, the prohibition of the substitution of *ṇ* for *n* is established due to the intervention of a *pada*.
Otherwise, because the condition of being a suffix (*pratyayalaksana*) would be absent, there would be no intervention of a *pada* between the cause (*nimitta*) and the effect (*nimittin*).

[Objection: But surely here too, even though it is not a word (*pada*), its status as a word will be established by the rule for the application of suffixes (*pratyayalakṣaṇa*) through the force of the particle *iti*.
[Reply: It is said:
if the determination were based on such force, then the objection raised regarding the stated manner would be fruitless.

Now, if—starting from the rule *sātpadādyoḥ* and based on the statement *kārye 'padādividhau*—the status of being a *pada* (*padatvam*) applies to the subsequent element, then in rules such as *bhāvakarmaṇoḥ*, where one ought to apply the condition *padāntasya* regarding the prohibition of *ṇatva*, the status of being a *pada* would be attained; consequently, there would have to be a prohibition of *ṇatva* by virtue of the rule *padāntasya*.
To this, it is replied:
There is no fault, because of the rule's formulation as "bhāvakarmaṇoḥ.
But if [the rule] "uttarapadatve cāpadādividhau" applies,
then how is it that we have the form *vimaladyu dinam*?

To this extent, even here, because of the rule stating "and when there is the designation of the latter member [of a compound] and the designation of not being the beginning of a word" (*apadādividhau*), the word *div* does not possess the status of being a *pada*.
It is replied: in that context, the term *anta* ("end") from the rule *eṅaḥ padāntādati* is understood to carry over (*anuvartate*).

By that rule regarding the final element (*tadantavidhi*), the substitution of *u* for the vowel of the word *div-* at the end of a compound is established, as in *vimaladyu dinam* ("a day with a clear sky").

However, in cases where the word is used alone, such as *dyubhyām*, the substitution of *u* occurs by virtue of the principle of "behaving like that which possesses a designation" (*vyapadeśivadbhāva*).
And it is not the case that this principle of "behaving like that which possesses a designation" does not apply when the word is not part of a compound beginning with *pra*.
Because of the mention [of the directions] in the rule "dyuprāgapāgudakpratīco yat" (Pāṇini 5.3.28). || 101 ||
With the disappearance of the cause, there is also the disappearance of that which is caused by it. || 102 ||
That which is produced by a cause is "caused" (*naimittika*).
[The suffix] *ṭhak* is applied here according to the rule for *vuñ*, *chaṇ*, etc., due to its inclusion in the *kumuda* group.
When the cause ceases, its effect also ceases.
Therefore, in the case of *snāti*, the absence of the retroflex nasal (*mūrdhanya*) causes the substitution of *ṇ* to disappear;
and in the case of *paṭubhārya*, upon the cessation of the feminine suffix *ṅīp*, the *yaṇ*-substitution is also reverted.

And there is an indicator (*jñāpaka*) for this: in rules such as *udaḥ sthāstambhoḥ pūrvasya*, the pronunciation of the letter *th* in place of *ṭh* [indicates that the rule applies even when the *ṣ* has been removed].
Furthermore, this worldly maxim is subject to exceptions;
for in the world, when a *japā* flower is near, the red color appears in the crystal, and when that [flower] is removed, the color ceases.
Furthermore, even in the absence of a carpenter, the palace still exists;
therefore, when the base [prakṛti] has departed, the suffix does not cease to apply, as in the case of "this is his offspring.

Likewise, in expressions such as *abhūn nṛpaḥ* ("there was a king"), during the grammatical refinement (*saṃskāra*) of the word, the *luṅ* suffix does not cease to apply once the past tense in general has been understood, even at the stage when the non-recent past (*anadyatana*) is being specifically apprehended.

In this *pāda*, regarding the rule *upasargādasamāse’pi ṇopadeśasya*, even under the view that there is doubling (*dvirvacana*) in place of [the single substitute], grammatical operations proceed by determining the identity [of the reduplicated form] with the original because there is no difference in its audible form (*śruti*). Thus, the objection and resolution—concerning the recitation of roots such as *sic* which are taught with an initial *s* (e.g., for the purpose of the prohibition in *sico yaṅi*)—are stated in the *Saṃprasāraṇa-bhāṣya* within the *Ekāc-pāda*.
Thus ends the third *pāda*, the *Repha-pāda*, in the *Paribhāṣāvṛtti*.
Thus ends the eighth chapter. || 8 || 8 ||
